subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a modular `scripts/install.sh` architecture now, and if so what public entrypoint and helper-loading shape must be preserved?
rationale: This is not a broken current behavior; it changes a stable public setup surface whose docs, website sync, tests, and release validation currently assume one shell script.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded split
options.body: Approve a module layout only if `openclaw.ai/install.sh` remains the safe public entrypoint and the publish/test matrix is updated in the same plan.

options.title: Keep targeted refactors only
options.body: Use this as backlog context and extract or delete installer sections only when tied to concrete bugs or validation improvements.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decide that the served shell installer should remain monolithic to avoid helper-loading and `curl | bash` packaging risk.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a guarded split
recommendation.body: Approve a module layout only if `openclaw.ai/install.sh` remains the safe public entrypoint and the publish/test matrix is updated in the same plan.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent installer-specific fixes and shell-helper refactors make this the strongest available routing signal for deciding whether the split shape is worth the compatibility cost.
